description: Beef ribs marinated with lemon and garlic, grilled over charcoal until charred and tender—Kenya's iconic barbecue dish.

steps.instruction: Mix lemon juice, crushed garlic, oil and salt. Rub over beef ribs and marinate for 20 minutes.
Grill over medium charcoal or barbecue for 30–40 minutes, turning occasionally, until charred and cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes, cut into pieces and serve with kachumbari.

description: Hearty beef ribs slow-cooked in a rich tomato and onion gravy until fall-off-the-bone tender.

steps.instruction: Boil beef ribs in salted water for 45–60 minutes until tender. Reserve broth.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add boiled ribs and reserved broth. Simmer for 20–30 minutes until sauce coats the ribs. Serve hot.

description: Boiled beef ribs stir-fried in a thick tomato and onion sauce—a hearty Kenyan wet fry.

steps.instruction: Boil beef ribs in salted water for 45–50 minutes until tender. Reserve broth.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes and cook until thick.
Add boiled ribs and a splash of broth. Stir-fry for 10–15 minutes until coated and sauce thickens.

description: Fragrant Kenyan pilau rice cooked with tender beef ribs, pilau masala and caramelised onions.

steps.instruction: Boil beef ribs for 45 minutes until tender. Reserve broth.
Fry onions until deep golden. Add pilau masala and ribs, stir. Add rice and coat.
Add broth and water, season with salt. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Fluff and serve.

description: Tender beef tripe slow-cooked in a rich tomato-onion gravy—a beloved Kenyan comfort dish.

steps.instruction: Clean tripe and boil in salted water for 1 to 1.5 hours until very tender. Cut into strips.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add tripe and stir to coat. Simmer for 10–15 minutes, adding water if needed. Season and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and sukuma wiki.

description: Boiled tripe stir-fried with onions, tomatoes and curry powder—a flavourful Kenyan delicacy.

steps.instruction: Clean and boil tripe in salted water for 1 to 1.5 hours until tender. Cut into strips.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic, curry powder and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add tripe and stir-fry for 5–10 minutes until well coated and heated through. Serve hot.

description: Tender tripe simmered in a creamy coconut and tomato sauce, a coastal Kenyan variation.

steps.instruction: Boil cleaned tripe in salted water for 1 to 1.5 hours until tender. Cut into strips.
Sauté onion until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add tripe and coconut milk. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Season and serve with rice.

description: Tripe and beans simmered together in a tomato-onion sauce, a protein-rich Kenyan stew.

steps.instruction: Boil cleaned tripe in salted water for 1 to 1.5 hours until tender. Cut into strips.
Sauté onion until golden, add tomatoes and cook until saucy. Add beans and tripe.
Simmer for 10–15 minutes, season and serve with ugali.

description: Sweet triangular fried dough from the Kenyan coast, perfumed with ground cardamom and coconut milk.

steps.instruction: Mix flour, cardamom, sugar and salt. Add coconut milk and knead into a soft dough.
Rest for 20 minutes. Roll out and cut into triangles.
Fry in hot oil for 2–3 minutes per side until golden. Drain and serve warm.

description: A warming Kenyan tea brewed with cardamom pods, milk and sugar.

steps.instruction: Crush cardamom pods and boil with water for 2 minutes.
Add tea leaves, milk and sugar. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Strain into cups and serve hot.

description: A creamy Kenyan rice pudding scented with cardamom, slow-cooked in milk and sweetened with sugar.

steps.instruction: Rinse rice and combine with milk in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then simmer on low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often, until creamy.
Stir in sugar and cardamom. Serve warm or chilled.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a dessert or snack.

description: Chicken pieces simmered with cardamom, onions and tomatoes, giving a warm, aromatic Kenyan stew.

steps.instruction: Brown chicken in oil for 6–8 minutes.
Add onion and cook until soft. Stir in cardamom and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add salt and water, cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Serve with rice.

description: Fresh green beans simmered in a creamy coconut curry with tomatoes and mild spices—a coastal Kenyan side.

steps.instruction: Trim green beans. Sauté onion until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add green beans and coconut milk.
Simmer for 10–12 minutes until beans are tender. Season and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or grilled fish.

description: A colourful Kenyan stir-fry of green beans and carrots, lightly seasoned and perfect alongside ugali.

steps.instruction: Trim green beans and slice carrots into strips.
Sauté onion in oil until soft. Add carrots and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add green beans and salt, stir-fry for 6–8 minutes until tender. Serve hot.

description: Green beans and potatoes simmered in a tomato-onion sauce, a hearty Kenyan side or main.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion until golden, add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add cubed potatoes and water, simmer for 15 minutes.
Add green beans and salt, cook for 8 minutes. Serve.

description: Green beans sautéed with onions and scrambled eggs, a quick Kenyan breakfast or light meal.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion in oil until soft. Add chopped green beans and cook for 5 minutes.
Beat eggs with salt and pour over the beans.
Scramble until eggs are set. Serve with chapati.

name_sw: Saladi ya Tango na Maziwa ya Mgando
description: A refreshing Kenyan salad of cucumber, yogurt, mint and a hint of garlic.

steps.instruction: Grate cucumber and squeeze out excess water.
Mix yogurt, crushed garlic, chopped mint and salt.
Stir in cucumber and serve chilled.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a side with pilau or grilled meat.

description: Chicken pieces marinated in spiced yogurt, then grilled until juicy and charred.

steps.instruction: Mix yogurt, crushed garlic, paprika, oil and salt. Coat chicken and marinate for 20 minutes.
Grill over medium heat for 8–10 minutes per side until cooked through and charred.
Serve hot with kachumbari or rice.

name_sw: Smoothie ya Maziwa ya Mgando na Ndizi
description: A creamy, refreshing smoothie of yogurt and ripe bananas, a popular Kenyan breakfast or snack drink.

steps.instruction: Peel bananas and break into chunks.
Blend yogurt, bananas, milk (if using) and sugar until smooth.
Pour into glasses and serve chilled.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a breakfast drink or afternoon snack.

description: A cooling Kenyan rice dish mixed with creamy yogurt, cucumber and mint.

steps.instruction: Cook rice in salted water until tender. Cool slightly.
Mix yogurt with grated cucumber and chopped mint.
Fold in the rice and serve at room temperature or chilled.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a cooling side with spicy dishes.

description: A stiff maize flour porridge that is the staple food of Kenya, served with vegetables, meat or fish.

steps.instruction: Bring water and salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Gradually add maize flour while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat and keep stirring for 8–10 minutes until firm. Shape and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with sukuma wiki, beans or meat.

description: The quintessential Kenyan meal: stiff maize flour ugali served with sautéed collard greens.

steps.instruction: Boil water and salt, gradually add maize flour and stir until firm. Shape ugali.
Sauté onion in oil until golden. Add sliced collard greens and cook for 5–7 minutes.
Serve the hot ugali with the greens.

description: Stiff ugali served with a hearty bean stew, a filling and economical Kenyan meal.

steps.instruction: Prepare ugali by boiling water and salt, adding maize flour and stirring until firm.
Sauté onion until golden, add tomatoes and cook until saucy. Add beans and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve the bean stew with the hot ugali.

description: Stiff ugali served with traditional sour milk, a Kalenjin-inspired Kenyan combination.

steps.instruction: Boil water and salt, gradually add maize flour and stir until firm. Shape ugali.
Serve the hot ugali with chilled or room-temperature sour milk alongside.
Eat by dipping pieces of ugali into the sour milk.

description: Stiff ugali served with a rich Kenyan beef stew, the ultimate comfort meal.

steps.instruction: Boil beef until tender. Sauté onions in oil, add tomatoes and cook until saucy. Add beef and simmer.
Prepare ugali by boiling water and adding maize flour until firm.
Serve hot ugali with the beef stew.

description: Green grams cooked into a soft, flavorful stew with tomatoes and onions.

steps.instruction: Rinse green grams and boil in water for 30–40 minutes until soft.
Sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add cooked green grams with some liquid. Simmer for 10 minutes, season and serve.

description: Green grams simmered in creamy coconut milk with onions and mild spices—a coastal Kenyan favourite.

steps.instruction: Rinse green grams. Sauté onion and garlic until soft. Stir in curry powder.
Add green grams, coconut milk, water and salt.
Simmer for 20–25 minutes until grams are soft. Serve with rice.

description: A comforting Kenyan one-pot rice and green gram dish with onions and mild spices.

steps.instruction: Boil green grams in water for 20 minutes until almost tender.
Sauté onion until golden. Add rice, green grams, salt and water.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender. Fluff and serve.

description: Soft green grams cooked with plenty of onions until they melt into a savoury, comforting stew.

steps.instruction: Rinse green grams and boil in water for 25–30 minutes until soft.
Sauté onions until golden and sweet. Add tomatoes if using and cook until saucy.
Add cooked green grams with liquid. Simmer for 10 minutes, season and serve.

description: A rich, nutty stew made with groundnuts, tomatoes and onions—often served with rice or ugali.

steps.instruction: Roast groundnuts lightly, then grind into a paste.
Sauté onions until golden. Add tomatoes and cook until soft. Add groundnut paste and water, stir well.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes until thickened. Season and serve with rice or ugali.

description: Chicken pieces simmered in a rich, nutty groundnut sauce with onions, tomatoes, garlic and ginger.

steps.instruction: Roast groundnuts and grind into a paste. Brown chicken in oil and remove.
Sauté onions and garlic until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy. Add groundnut paste and water.
Return chicken and simmer for 25–30 minutes until cooked and sauce thickens. Season and serve.

description: A rich, nutty Kenyan stew of spinach simmered with groundnuts, tomatoes and onions.

steps.instruction: Roast groundnuts and grind into a coarse paste.
Sauté onion until golden. Add tomatoes and cook until softened. Add groundnut paste and water, stir.
Simmer for 8–10 minutes, add spinach and salt and cook for 5 minutes. Serve with rice or ugali.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice, ugali or chapati.

description: Rice cooked with groundnut paste and onions, a rich and nutty Kenyan side dish.

steps.instruction: Roast groundnuts and grind into a paste. Sauté onion in oil until soft.
Stir in groundnut paste and rice. Add water and salt.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender. Fluff and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with grilled fish or chicken.

description: A simple and nutritious Kenyan cabbage stew cooked with tomatoes and onions.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion in oil until soft and golden.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce.
Add shredded cabbage and salt. Stir, add water, cover and simmer for 10–15 minutes. Serve hot.

description: A quick, colourful Kenyan stir-fry of shredded cabbage and sweet carrot, lightly seasoned.

steps.instruction: Shred cabbage and grate or julienne carrots.
Heat oil and sauté onion until soft. Add carrots and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add cabbage and salt, stir-fry for 6–8 minutes until tender but crunchy. Serve.

description: Shredded cabbage stir-fried with minced beef and tomatoes, a quick Kenyan weeknight dish.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion until soft. Add minced beef and brown.
Add tomatoes and cook until saucy. Add shredded cabbage and salt.
Stir-fry for 8–10 minutes until cabbage is tender. Serve hot.

description: Cabbage and potatoes simmered in a tomato-onion sauce, a hearty Kenyan side or main.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion until golden, add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add cubed potatoes and water, simmer for 15 minutes.
Add shredded cabbage and salt, cook for 8 minutes. Serve hot.

description: Sautéed collard greens cooked with tomatoes and onions—Kenya's most popular everyday vegetable side dish.

steps.instruction: Wash collard greens, remove stems and slice thinly.
Heat oil and sauté onions until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add greens and salt, cook for 5–7 minutes until wilted but still bright. Serve with ugali.

description: Collard greens simmered in creamy coconut milk with onions—a coastal Kenyan side dish.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion in oil until soft. Add sliced collard greens and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and add salt.
Simmer for 7–10 minutes until greens are tender. Serve with rice.

description: Collard greens and beans simmered in a tomato-onion sauce, a protein-rich Kenyan stew.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion until golden, add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add beans and cook for 5 minutes.
Add sliced collard greens and salt, cook for 5–7 minutes. Serve with ugali.

description: Collard greens sautéed with onions and scrambled eggs, a nutritious Kenyan breakfast.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion in oil until soft. Add sliced collard greens and cook for 3 minutes.
Beat eggs with salt and pour over the greens.
Scramble until eggs are set. Serve with chapati.

description: Collard greens and potatoes simmered together in a tomato-onion sauce, a hearty Kenyan side or main.

steps.instruction: Peel and cube potatoes. Sauté onion until golden, add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add potatoes and water, simmer for 15 minutes until almost tender.
Add sliced collard greens and salt, cook for 5 minutes. Serve hot.
